title: Python and Spark SQL, together
brief_copy: Both are first-class for Lakehouse work, with connected Files and Tables in one dependency model.
description: Use Python and Spark SQL together to load files and create Lakehouse tables. Weaver runs the steps in the right order.

title: Ordinary T-SQL
brief_copy: Keep the SELECTs your team knows—without a proprietary modelling language or macros.
description: Keep ordinary SELECTs, without a proprietary modelling language or macros.

title: Keep using Power BI files
brief_copy: Keep PBIP, TMDL and Report definitions. No conversion to a Weaver-only modelling format.
description: Apply modelling standards, run unit tests and deploy Reports using standard Power BI project files (PBIP and TMDL).

title: Work in Fabric or your own editor
brief_copy: Build and operate the same project through the desktop CLI/Python API or an attached Fabric notebook.
description: Write code in VS Code or another editor on Windows, macOS or Linux, or work entirely in Fabric Notebooks. Deploy native Power BI models and Reports without Power BI Desktop.

title: Built for developers and AI agents
brief_copy: Readable terminal output and structured --json results, with previews, validation and explicit outcomes, for developers and AI agents.
description: Use readable terminal output or structured JSON results from Check, Build, Load, Test and Health. The guide shows how to give an agent a development workspace, preview changes and run without prompts.

title: Keep work in the right order
brief_copy: Connect Lakehouse Files, Python and Spark SQL work to Warehouse T-SQL and dependent semantic-model refreshes in one dependency graph.
description: Run Lakehouse work, Warehouse SQL and dependent Power BI model refreshes in one connected workflow.
qualification: Cycles use deterministic once-per-invocation ordering, not iteration to convergence. Runtime evidence: efc046e7cf066daefd27f9268413ae05c3ed64e4 src/weaver/graph.py. Historical documentation hashes below retain their original provenance.

title: Turn a SQL query into a working table
brief_copy: A SELECT becomes a physical Table with generated staging, key matching, row-change reconciliation and recorded results.
description: Give Weaver a SELECT and a key. It creates the table and loading steps, tracks changes and records the results.

title: Turn Python and SQL into Lakehouse tables
brief_copy: Files, Python and Spark SQL materialise into managed Delta Tables without hand-building a separate orchestration project.
description: Use Python and Spark SQL to load files and update Delta Tables, without building a separate pipeline to connect them.

title: Find what depends on what
brief_copy: Python imports and supported T-SQL references supply dependencies; explicit declarations cover other cases.
description: Weaver can read dependencies from Python imports and supported T-SQL references. With Spark SQL, you specify them.

title: Load only what has changed
brief_copy: Apply supported changes without reconstructing every target; source logic identifies candidates and explicit deletes.
description: Apply inserts, updates and explicit deletes using rules you choose, without rebuilding every target.

title: Pick up where each table left off
brief_copy: Each consumer retains its own successful processing position—even when multiple Tables read the same source.
description: Each table or folder tracks its own progress through the source data, even when several share the same source.
qualification: Named Table/Folder ownership; a clean successful boundary rather than arbitrary source watermark.

title: Test data and calculations
brief_copy: Compare expected and actual results, or catch rows that violate a rule, in Python, SQL and DAX.
description: Compare actual and expected results or find invalid rows using Python, SQL and DAX.

title: Data-quality safeguards
brief_copy: Track rejected rows and use stability thresholds to stop unusually large changes before they are applied.
description: Keep rejected rows and stop unusually large proposed updates or deletes before they reach your tables.

title: Organisation-wide modelling standards
brief_copy: Apply shared TMDL policy across models instead of repeating formats and conventions manually.
description: Apply shared native TMDL policy across Semantic Models instead of repeating formats and conventions.

title: Built-in modelling rules
brief_copy: Hide foreign keys, organise measures and apply supported model rules through native TMDL declarations.
description: Automatically hide foreign keys and create measure selectors using standard TMDL annotations.
qualification: Replaced broad organise-measures wording with supported generated measure-selector behaviour.

title: Write your own modelling rules in Python
brief_copy: Write a project-specific modelling convention when native policy and built-ins aren't enough.
description: Add your own Python rules when you need more than Weaver's built-in modelling options.

title: Reuse models without copying them
brief_copy: Reuse a shared model foundation to produce variants for different audiences without copying everything.
description: Start from a shared model and create versions for different audiences without maintaining complete copies.

title: Unit testing for Semantic Models
brief_copy: Independently validate measures, including comparisons against calculations over managed Lakehouse or Warehouse sources.
description: Unit test DAX measures against independent expected results, including SQL calculations over managed Lakehouse or Warehouse sources.

title: Connect Reports to the right models
brief_copy: Deploy one authored Report to different targets, resolving and checking the intended model and workspace binding.
description: Deploy the same Report to different workspaces. Weaver checks that it connects to the intended Power BI model.

title: See all your work in one place
brief_copy: Queryable installed definitions, signatures, metadata, dependencies and operational state in a Fabric Warehouse.
description: Weaver keeps its Catalogue of deployed items, dependencies and run results in an ordinary Fabric Warehouse. There's no separate monitoring service to run.

title: See what is up to date or needs attention
brief_copy: See current, stale, pending, failed or inconsistent work across the registered managed estate.
description: See what is up to date, waiting, failed or inconsistent across your managed Fabric work.

title: See run history and results
brief_copy: Inspect workflow history, Load counts, timings, row changes and recorded outcomes.
description: See what ran, how long it took, row counts, data changes and recorded results.

title: Keep a failed step from stopping unrelated work
brief_copy: Preserve completed work; record failures and blocked dependants; optionally continue independent Load branches.
description: Choose fault-tolerant loading to let independent branches continue after a failure. Completed changes remain in place; inspect the failed step before retrying it.

title: Run a table, a branch or an item
brief_copy: Select installed work by whole-name regex, add ancestors/descendants deliberately, and preview the plan.
description: Preview the work you intend to run. Select an item for its ordered loads, or name an object and explicitly include the upstream or downstream work you need.

title: Run independent branches together
brief_copy: Limit one invocation or tune per-resource work; schedule independent work without breaking dependency ordering.
description: Set concurrency limits for the run and its resources. Weaver can overlap independent Spark and Warehouse work while keeping dependent steps in order.

title: One project, multiple environments
brief_copy: Keep logical identities and source files; map physical item and model destinations through workspace configuration.
description: Use the same files in development and production. A configuration file sets which workspaces, Fabric items and Power BI models they belong to.

title: Update only what changed
brief_copy: Detect changed definitions and affected installed descendants; leave certified unchanged work in place.
description: Update changed source definitions and the work that depends on them, while leaving unchanged parts in place.
qualification: Limited unchanged-work claim to source-data Build; selected models redeploy even unchanged.

title: See changes before applying them
brief_copy: See selected actions, physical targets and destructive effects before running Build.
description: Preview what will change, where it will go and whether anything will be replaced or deleted.

title: Review deployments before applying them
brief_copy: Review and hand off frozen, destination-specific installation plans without replanning them during Install.
description: Prepare a fixed deployment plan, review it and apply it later without changing the plan.

title: Coordinate the hand-off between engines
brief_copy: Handle supported Lakehouse publication and SQL endpoint-readiness barriers before dependent Warehouse consumers execute.
description: When your Warehouse reads a loaded Lakehouse table, Weaver waits for its SQL endpoint refresh. A shortcut reading another team's Warehouse table also waits for the source's OneLake publication.

title: Protect important data
brief_copy: Separate source ownership from managed targets, preserve protected objects and bound destructive operations.
description: Keep irreplaceable sources outside managed targets and use Build replacement guards for protected owned objects.
qualification: Build replacement guard is not protection from Load, Wipe or re-Mirror.

title: Share a Session across Python operations
brief_copy: A workflow shares Session and configuration; Load and Test records correlate under its workflow ID.
description: A workflow shares Session and configuration; Load and Test records correlate under its workflow ID.
qualification: Reviewed against runtime efc046e7cf066daefd27f9268413ae05c3ed64e4; documentation is a forthcoming-release draft.
surface_reason: Removed notebook Session-sharing card at Matthias’s request; API remains in developer reference.

title: Query your Fabric data from the terminal
brief_copy: Exactly one command or file is submitted. SQL and Python can mutate data; Weaver does not automatically create Load or Test records.
description: Use weaver execute to inspect a Warehouse, Lakehouse or model with T-SQL, Spark SQL, Python or DAX. Read the results without switching tools. Submitted SQL and Python can also change data.
qualification: Reviewed against runtime efc046e7cf066daefd27f9268413ae05c3ed64e4; documentation is a forthcoming-release draft.

title: Catch up after a source changes
brief_copy: Test stale selection is distinct from the pre-existing Load stale selection.
description: Use load --stale to rerun loads that need attention, then test --stale for validations that are no longer current. You can recover the affected work without repeating the whole project.
qualification: Reviewed against runtime efc046e7cf066daefd27f9268413ae05c3ed64e4; documentation is a forthcoming-release draft.

title: Connect the work without merging the projects
brief_copy: Catalogues supply context; item or workspace selection determines which work runs.
description: Supply the catalogues for the teams involved. Health follows their recorded dependencies; Load and Test coordinate the work you select and write each result to its owning catalogue.
qualification: Reviewed against runtime efc046e7cf066daefd27f9268413ae05c3ed64e4; documentation is a forthcoming-release draft.

title: Keep reciprocal team dependencies workable
brief_copy: Deterministic once-per-invocation ordering, not iteration to convergence.
description: If teams read each other's results, Weaver reports the cycle and runs selected objects once in a consistent order. A reader closing the loop uses the producer's available result from an earlier run.
qualification: Reviewed against runtime efc046e7cf066daefd27f9268413ae05c3ed64e4; documentation is a forthcoming-release draft.

title: Several teams on one Dashboard
brief_copy: Up to ten Direct Lake catalogues; Import supports more than ten and requires refresh.
description: One Dashboard can read several teams' catalogues, show which workspaces supply which, and narrow every page by workspace, item and object in the Filters pane.
qualification: Reviewed against runtime efc046e7cf066daefd27f9268413ae05c3ed64e4; documentation is a forthcoming-release draft.

title: Static pages for sharing
brief_copy: A snapshot reflects model data at export; a downloaded local file opens without Fabric capacity. Lakehouse destinations still need access.
description: Export a snapshot of the deployed model's data as HTML, from the CLI or a notebook. A downloaded local copy opens without a running Fabric capacity.
qualification: Reviewed against runtime efc046e7cf066daefd27f9268413ae05c3ed64e4; documentation is a forthcoming-release draft.
